subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp-artifact provenance and cleanup model, and if so should the core scope be limited to runtime/doctor guardrails plus a SQLite-backed provenance seam while workflow-specific classifications live in plugins or ClawHub?
rationale: The safety goal fits current priorities, but the requested behavior crosses core storage policy, agent/tool APIs, cleanup authority, doctor/runtime guardrails, and plugin-vs-core ownership.

options.title: Core Guardrails Plus Plugin Seam
options.body: Core would add runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance contract, leaving audit/review classification policy to plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full Core Provenance Registry
options.body: Core would own artifact classes, cleanup and janitor semantics, promotion paths, and broad first-class temp artifact metadata for agent-created files.

options.title: Track Only Narrow Bugs
options.body: Decline the broad provenance model and keep only concrete runtime temp-path failures or store-specific cleanup bugs as separate issues.

recommendation.title: Core Guardrails Plus Plugin Seam
recommendation.body: Core would add runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance contract, leaving audit/review classification policy to plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This person already made the closest related ClawHub scope call and has relevant temp-boundary hardening history.
